# k0rdent Provider

Manages k0rdent AI infrastructure through the k0rdent AI API.

Credentials are read from the environment and cannot be set here — see the provider documentation for why, and for how to obtain a service account.

A few values still have to be written as literals, because no read a tenant credential can make supplies them. The [hardcoded values](guides/hardcoded-values.md) guide names each known gap and the side that has to change.

## Example Usage

```terraform
terraform {
  required_providers {
    k0rdent = {
      source = "k0rdent/k0rdent"
    }
  }
}

# Every argument is optional and falls back to an environment variable, so a
# pipeline can use an empty block.
provider "k0rdent" {
  # Scheme and host only, without /v1. Falls back to K0RDENT_ENDPOINT.
  endpoint = "https://api.k0rdent.ai"

  # List regions with `k0rdent_regions`. Falls back to K0RDENT_REGION.
  region = "us-texas-1"

  # The project's id. Falls back to K0RDENT_PROJECT.
  project = "cp-production"

  # Tags for every cluster, network, security group and VPC peering. A
  # resource's own `tags` win over these. A VPC peering only gets them when
  # it's created.
  default_tags = {
    cost-center = "ml-platform"
    managed-by  = "terraform"
  }

  # There's no credential argument. Set a service account in the environment:
  #
  #   export K0RDENT_CLIENT_ID='sa-terraform@example.iam'
  #   read -rs K0RDENT_CLIENT_SECRET && export K0RDENT_CLIENT_SECRET
  #
  # read -rs keeps the secret out of your shell history.
  #
  # K0RDENT_API_KEY also works, with a warning: it stops working when the
  # person who created it leaves.
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `default_tags` (Map of String) Tags for every resource this provider manages that carries `tags`. Each of those resources shows the result in its computed `tags_all`: these with the resource's own `tags` on top, a resource tag winning over a default with the same key. Changing one here updates each resource in place, and removing one removes it, except on a VPC peering, whose tags the API sets only at creation. A value that isn't known until apply is allowed. It leaves `tags_all` unknown in the plan, so every cluster, network and security group plans an in-place update, and at apply one whose tags come out the same as before sends nothing. A VPC peering plans nothing. The key `terraform-provider-k0rdent/create-token` is the provider's own and is refused.
- `endpoint` (String) Base URL of the k0rdent AI API, for example `https://api.k0rdent.ai`. Falls back to the `K0RDENT_ENDPOINT` environment variable, then to `https://api.k0rdent.ai`, which is the contract's declared server and has not been verified against any landscape.
- `operation_timeout` (String) How long to wait for an asynchronous change — a cluster create, a scale, a destroy — to settle before giving up. A Go duration string such as `45m`. Falls back to the `K0RDENT_OPERATION_TIMEOUT` environment variable, then to `2h0m0s`.

Unset, a cluster's and an instance group's create and delete wait up to `3h` instead, because building or freeing hardware can take more than 2 hours. Set, it applies to those too.

A wait that runs out stops nothing on the platform. A create that stops waiting fails and Terraform taints it: `terraform untaint` and then `terraform apply` wait for it. A delete that stops waiting stays in state, and the next `terraform destroy` waits for it.
- `poll_interval` (String) How often to re-read a resource while waiting for it to settle. A Go duration string such as `10s`. Falls back to the `K0RDENT_POLL_INTERVAL` environment variable, then to `10s`.
- `project` (String) Project slug for project-scoped resources, used as the `{project}` URL segment. Falls back to the `K0RDENT_PROJECT` environment variable. This is the project's `id`, as the `k0rdent_projects` data source reports it. Optional, because the region-wide catalogs are not project-scoped.
- `region` (String) Region id for regional resources, used as the `{region}` URL segment. Falls back to the `K0RDENT_REGION` environment variable. Ids are operator-declared and deployment-specific; read them from `GET /v1/regions`, where each entry's `id` is this value. It's also the region a new `k0rdent_project` defaults to, so in practice it's the region your project lives in. `global` is the control-plane tier, which the provider addresses on its own for authentication and IAM, and is a region only on an installation that runs compute under it, where the regions list reports it with `hosts_projects`. Optional, because discovering a valid id requires a configured provider.
